jobs.title: Test Automation Engineer, Hardware-in-the-Loop
jobs.description_text: The Role Applied Physical Systems is a small, cross-functional engineering team at Hadrian. We build technology that spans more than one manufacturing capability, needs hardware and software designed together, and can't be bought off the shelf. We take a solution from proof of concept through prototype to a first production-ready version, then hand it to the teams that run it at scale. Engineers on the team design, build and commission their own systems on the factory floor. You will build the test infrastructure that lets engineers and AI agents check hardware the way software teams check code. Your work will span designing and wiring test stands, writing the frameworks and CI that run them, and analyzing results from unattended test campaigns. You will work with the mechatronics, robotics, firmware and controls engineers whose systems run on your benches, and with software teams on CI and test data. You will also decide which questions need the bench and which ones simulation can answer. jobs.title: Director, Forward Deployed Supply Chain
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: The Director, Forward Deployed Supply Chain leads the supply chain arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside the Supply Chain organization and partner directly with Customer Programs on new customer engagements. The scope covers three streams: scoping the supply side of what Hadrian builds for customers, mapping customer demand across commodities so it becomes a planning input to our factories and supply base, and designing supply chain as a service solutions where Hadrian runs part of the customer's supply chain on their behalf. You work directly with customers every day, and for many of them you are the face of Hadrian supply chain. The work starts with discovery: getting inside the customer's operation, mapping their demand, bill of material, and supply base, and understanding what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for. From there, you steer to the solution where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other, built on suppliers, agreements, and capabilities we already have. The accountability is clear: your team scopes what we commit to, and the Supply Chain organization delivers it. Commitments have to be grounded in real demand, supplier capacity, lead times, and cost, not optimism. jobs.description_text: WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue. The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive. The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Architect the system. jobs.title: Senior Technical Writer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE: Our docs get used in a few different ways. Some people land on a page in the middle of a task and just need the answer. Others are working out how to run Kong across a whole company, with real traffic and a lot of teams. The docs also power agent workflows, ours and our customers', like MCP servers and AI assistants. So when a page is wrong, it's wrong everywhere. You'll own the docs for at least one product area, and you'll decide what to work on based on what you see. What features are releasing? Where are people getting stuck? What are the field teams hearing? You won't spend all your time in your area, though. You'll work with the other docs writers every day, check in with them when your work is done, ask for help when you're buried, and weigh in on each other's problems. You'll also work closely with product managers and engineers, and you'll be in their conversations early. We own our docs platform, too. If a workflow could be better, you can build a better one. Add Vale rules, upgrade the platform, set up auto-generated docs. We have a docs engineer that can help you turn your needs into real features! WHAT YOU'LL DO: Own your product area - Own the documentation strategy for your area. That means getting into the product, seeing what's about to ship, deciding what needs writing, and planning the work. Share that plan with the docs team so everyone knows what's in motion. jobs.description_text: The Role Mariana Minerals is looking for an experienced Pilot Plant Operations Manager to lead operations at our DSM Pilot Plant in Houston. The DSM pilot is a first-of-its-kind, fully integrated flowsheet that couples a high temperature pyrometallurgical section with a downstream hydrometallurgical refining section. You will own safe, reliable, round-the-clock operation of both sections and lead the technician team that runs them. This is a highly hands-on leadership role. You will build the operating team from the ground up, take the plant through commissioning and startup, and then run structured campaigns that generate the process data and product samples the company depends on. You will work shoulder to shoulder with process engineers, R&D scientists, maintenance, and the analytical laboratory, and you will be accountable for the safety, quality, and throughput of everything that happens on the floor. The role reports to the Houston site leadership team and carries direct responsibility for people, budgets for consumables and spares, shift structure, and operational readiness. You will set the safety culture for a plant that handles hot solids, molten material, combustion systems, process off-gas, concentrated acids and bases, and organic solvents. What You Will Do - Lead the DSM pilot operations team, including shift leads and technicians across the pyrometallurgy and hydrometallurgy sections. jobs.title: Sr. Cost Control Engineer
jobs.description_text: The role We are hiring a Cost Control Engineer to own the cost baseline, the forecast, and change control on Mariana's capital projects. You will build the cost breakdown structure, convert the sanctioned estimate into a control budget, track commitments and actuals, and produce the forecast at completion that the business plans against. The role sits between engineering, procurement, construction, and finance — the path where a commitment becomes an accrual becomes an invoice becomes a capitalized asset — and your job is to make sure the number is the same in all four places. Cost control here is not a monthly report assembled by hand. The reporting is expected to come out of the system and building that pipeline is as much the job as running it. What you'll do - Set the baseline. Build the WBS and cost breakdown structure with the planner and estimator, convert the sanctioned estimate into a control budget, and lock it - Track commitments and actuals. Purchase orders, subcontracts, change orders, and field costs, reconciled to the ERP every month with no unexplained variance - Forecast. Maintain estimate to complete and estimate at completion by control account, with the basis for each forecast written down rather than carried in your head - Measure earned value. Set rules of credit with the planner, measure physical progress, and report cost and schedule performance at a level where someone can act on it - Run the trend and change process. jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. As Engineering Manager, Compiler & Runtime, you will build and lead the team that writes the core of it: the compiler that takes PyTorch models to our hardware, the runtime that executes them, and the kernels in between. This is a people-leadership role on a technical team. You will hire the team, plan its work against the hardware program, and partner with our senior compiler architect, who sets the team's technical direction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so the team builds against simulators and FPGA prototypes first. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - Team Building: Grow the compiler and runtime team from its first engineers, set the hiring bar, and develop each engineer's growth and career. - Delivery: Turn the Systems Software roadmap into plans, milestones, and staffing for the compiler, runtime, and kernels, and deliver against them. Success means LLMs run end to end on our hardware through PyTorch. - Technical Partnership: Work with our compiler architect so that technical decisions get made, staffed, and finished. jobs.description_text: THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication. Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes. THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip. jobs.title: Product Manager | Bill Pay
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Every business pays bills, and many of them still do it by hand. Someone opens the invoice, types it in, codes it, chases approvals, pays it, matches it and syncs it to the books. It's one of the largest manual workflows left in finance. We're building the version where software does that work. Bills come in and get read, coded, matched, approved and paid, and a person steps in only when judgment matters. Bill Pay is already one of Ramp's fastest-growing products. The next few years decide who owns AP for the next decade, and we plan for it to be us. We're looking for a PM who wants to build that. - Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week. - Level will be determined based on the candidate’s interview performance and previous scope of responsibility. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own strategy, roadmap and results for a major part of Bill Pay. - Spend real time with AP clerks, controllers and CFOs, and turn what you see into product. - Prototype with customers, set quality bars with Engineering and Data, and ship automation people trust. - Measure success by adoption, automation and time saved, then use the data to decide what comes next. - Work with Procurement, Accounting, Payments and Risk so a bill moves from inbox to payment to the books without gaps. Stack prepares reviewable work so the customer's team keeps accounting judgment and approval. As a Stack Account Executive, you'll sell to finance and accounting leaders (Controllers, VPs of Accounting, CFOs) in a new, fast-moving product motion. You'll hear how a team actually closes the books, find the recurring manual step that creates drag, and turn it into a focused proof path and a commercial plan. jobs.title: FinOps Specialist, Production Engineering
jobs.description_text: Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You'll have the opportunity to build from 0–1 and scale from 1–100, bringing new AI products to life and turning early traction into lasting customer value. jobs.description_text: Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench. As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper. - Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency. - Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail. - Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously. - Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems. - Work with researchers and engineers across Sierr

This role sits at the intersection of IT and production, ensuring that critical systems—such as Zebra printers, barcode scanners, production workstations, and manufacturing applications—operate reliably and efficiently. You will be a key IT partner to manufacturing, and operations teams, supporting day-to-day production activities while driving continuous improvement in systems, processes, and uptime. RESPONSIBILITIES - Provide frontline and escalated support for manufacturing systems and operational technology, including Zebra printers (ZPL configuration and troubleshooting), barcode scanners, production-floor workstations and displays, shop-floor networking, and connected IoT devices. - Troubleshoot and resolve hardware, software, application, and network issues impacting production, with urgency and precision to minimize downtime. - Act as a primary responder for manufacturing system incidents and coordinate cross-functional resolution efforts when necessary. - Support data-related tasks and production workflows, including basic query troubleshooting (SQL, Splunk; Python is a plus). - Coordinate IT support with the broader IT team. - Maintain knowledge base articles and support documentation for supported systems and processes. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer – Electrical
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW The Manufacturing Engineer – Electrical Detail Planning translates electrical system designs, equipment arrangements, and wire connection data into the detailed work instructions used to install electrical equipment, route and pull cable, and complete terminations aboard autonomous surface vessels. This role covers both the physical hardware side of electrical installation and the planning required to turn a wire connection list into a buildable installation strategy. Electrical installation in shipbuilding depends on foundations, wireways, and penetrations being planned and installed at the correct stage of construction, and on cable routing being translated from a connection list into a real physical path through the ship. The Manufacturing Engineer ensures this translation happens accurately and efficiently, minimizing rework and schedule risk. This role works closely with design engineering, structural and outfitting planning, and waterfront production to ensure electrical installation work is sequenced correctly and executable by the trades. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer – Structural Detail Planning
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW The Manufacturing Engineer – Structural Detail Planning defines how a vessel's structure is built, from individual parts and plates through subassemblies, units, blocks, grand blocks, and the complete erected hull. This role establishes the build strategy and detailed work instructions that govern structural fabrication and assembly, and ensures secondary structure and foundations are installed and welded at the correct stage of construction. Shipbuilding depends on a well-sequenced structural build strategy to control distortion, maintain fairness, and avoid rework as assemblies grow in size and complexity. The Manufacturing Engineer ensures breakdown strategy, fit-up sequence, and secondary structure integration are planned correctly so outfitting trades are never blocked by structure that wasn't ready. This role works closely with design engineering, piping, electrical, HVAC, and outfitting planning teams, as well as production and facilities, to build a structural plan the yard can actually execute. RESPONSIBILITIES - Build Strategy & Breakdown Planning ● Develop the build strategy breaking the hull into its construction hierarchy: parts, panels/subassemblies, units/blocks, grand blocks, and erected hull. ● Define breakdown (block boundary) locations based on facility constraints, crane/transport capacity, access, and weld/outfitting sequence. ● Specify fit-up, alignment, and weld sequence at each level of assembly to control distortion and accuracy. Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions for any production issues - Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities for continuous improvement in manufacturing processes and implement changes to enhance efficiency. Stay abreast of industry trends and emerging technologies to incorporate advancements into the manufacturing process - Documentation and Compliance: Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for manufacturing processes, ensuring compliance with industry regulations and standards. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer – Piping & HVAC Detail Planning
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW The Manufacturing Engineer – Piping & HVAC Detail Planning translates piping and HVAC system designs into the detailed, shop-floor-ready work instructions that production teams use to fabricate, assemble, and install these systems aboard autonomous surface vessels. This role defines how piping and HVAC systems are broken into spools and subassemblies, how those pieces are built and installed in sequence, and how they ultimately come together into a complete, functioning ship. Shipbuilding requires piping and HVAC systems to be planned around structural construction, access constraints, and the work of every other outfitting trade. The Manufacturing Engineer ensures fabrication and installation sequence, hanger and support design, and material handling are defined correctly the first time, minimizing rework and keeping systems installation on schedule. This role works closely with design engineering, scheduling, quality assurance, and waterfront production teams to translate engineering intent into buildable, station-by-station work packages. RESPONSIBILITIES Piping & HVAC Build Strategy - Break piping and HVAC systems into logical spools and subassemblies based on build strategy, weight handling limits, access, and outfitting sequence. - Define how subassemblies integrate into units, blocks, and the completed ship. - Determine fabrication sequence, hanger and support locations, and insulation/coating requirements. jobs.title: Sr. Field Service Quality Engineer
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW We are seeking an experienced and technically driven Senior Quality Engineer to lead quality initiatives supporting the manufacturing, integration, and delivery of complex electro-mechanical systems for autonomous surface vessels (ASVs). This role requires deep technical judgment, a strong understanding of design intent, structural integrity, and manufacturing processes, and extensive experience in root cause analysis, nonconformance management, and production support. As a senior member of the Quality team, you will serve as a technical authority on the production and integration floor, driving risk-based quality decisions, resolving complex technical issues, and partnering with Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain to ensure product integrity and operational excellence. The ideal candidate is comfortable navigating ambiguity in a fast-paced environment, influencing cross-functional teams, and balancing quality, safety, performance, and delivery requirements without compromising engineering standards. RESPONSIBILITIES - Lead Manufacturing Quality: Develop, implement, and continuously improve quality assurance processes, inspection strategies, and manufacturing controls. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer - Test Planner
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW The Test Planner defines and sequences all forms of testing required to bring a vessel from fabrication through commissioning and delivery, covering structural/tank testing, piping system testing, electrical testing, machinery and propulsion trials, and vessel-level dock and sea trials. This role establishes the master test plan that ties every discipline's test requirements into a single, logical sequence tied to the build schedule. Shipbuilding test programs span dozens of interdependent test types across structural, piping, electrical, HVAC, machinery, and outfitting systems, each with its own prerequisites, acceptance criteria, and regulatory requirements. The Test Planner ensures these tests happen in the right order, at the right stage of construction, without forcing rework or blocking downstream trades, and draws on experience from other shipyard programs to anticipate sequencing issues before they surface. This role works closely with design engineering, production engineering, quality assurance, classification society surveyors, and the Master Planner to build a test program the yard can execute reliably across multiple ship programs. jobs.title: Associate IT Systems Engineer
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW We are seeking a motivated, detail-oriented Associate Systems Engineer to support the day-to-day operation and maintenance of our infrastructure. Working under close guidance from senior engineers, you will help keep systems running reliably and securely across both on-premise and cloud environments. The ideal candidate has a foundational understanding of Windows and Linux systems, a strong desire to learn, and the discipline to follow established procedures carefully. You will carry out well-defined work such as patching, user provisioning, monitoring alert triage and backup verification. Along the way, you will build hands-on skills in virtualization, scripting, networking and cloud services. This role is ideal for an early-career engineer who wants to grow quickly in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. RESPONSIBILITIES - Perform day-to-day systems administration tasks across enterprise Windows and Linux environments, on-premise and in the cloud. - Apply operating system and application patches following established runbooks and change management procedures. - Provision, modify and deprovision user accounts and access in line with internal security policies. - Monitor system alerts, triage issues, and escalate problems that fall outside documented procedures or your training. - Perform routine backup verification and support restore testing as part of disaster recovery practices. - Shadow senior engineers on incident response, troubleshooting and small infra

jobs.title: Senior EHS Manager
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW The Senior EHS Manager owns the environmental, health, and safety program across Saronic's Austin operations, including office, production/manufacturing, and waterfront activities. You will build and lead a safety culture that protects our people while keeping pace with a fast-moving hardware and maritime environment. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will help the VP of EHS to set strategy and policy, but you will also be on the production floor and at the waterfront, coaching teams and solving problems in real time. Success means an organization where safe work is the fastest way to work, and where compliance is a baseline rather than a goal. jobs.title: Materials Systems & Process Manager
jobs.description_text: JOB OVERVIEW The Supply Chain Materials Systems & Process Manager owns how materials move, are recorded, and are taught across the enterprise, and leads the team that confirms every site is ready to run those processes. This role designs, standardizes, and scales materials management and warehouse processes, and serves as the subject matter expert (SME) for supply chain systems, inventory control, and warehouse operations. The Manager keeps physical material flow aligned with system execution in the ERP/WMS, and builds the training and certification programs that make that alignment repeatable at every site. The Manager also leads the Supply Training & Analysis Team, which develops curriculum, delivers and certifies training, and analyzes performance data to confirm readiness across Supply Chain Materials. RESPONSIBILITIES PROCESS AND SOP STANDARDIZATION Develop, publish, and maintain standardized SOPs for receiving, storage, inventory control, kitting, and replenishment. Drive enterprise-wide standardization so every site runs the same core processes, with documented, approved exceptions only. Manage SOP version control and change management so field practice and written procedure stay aligned. SYSTEMS ALIGNMENT (ERP/WMS) Align physical material flow with ERP/WMS transactions to ensure inventory accuracy and end-to-end traceability.
